verdict.rationale: OpenRouter documents automatic fallback when providers are down, rate-limited, or return errors. Users configure it with a priority-ordered `models` array, and provider load balancing is on by default, which community users corroborate. This is failover to alternate models or providers, not an explicitly configurable retry policy: nothing documents same-provider retries, retry counts, backoff, or per-error-class rules. missing for 10: configurable retry count/backoff settings, same-provider retry on transient errors, per-error-type retry rules, independent hands-on verification of retry behavior.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can set automatic retry policies for transient provider errors

citations.quote: The models parameter lets you automatically try other models if the primary model's providers are down, rate-limited, or refuse to reply due to content moderation.
Provide an array of model IDs in priority order. If the first model returns an error, OpenRouter will automatically try the next model in the list.
Fall back to other providers when one goes down.
They also support fallback by default so you don't have to write wrappers.
